thread.title: Flick and Hamm announce $25,000 grant for Lycoming Career and Technology Center
thread.title_full: Flick and Hamm announce $25,000 grant for Lycoming Career and Technology Center

author: a. j. garner
title: Flick and Hamm announce $25,000 grant for Lycoming Career and Technology Center
text:
Reps. Jamie Flick and Joe Hamm announced on May 20 that the Lycoming Career and Technology Center will receive a $25,000 grant to improve its training programs and provide students with updated equipment.
The funding is intended to help the school purchase new equipment, including an ironworker, for classrooms in a new training facility being built to meet increased enrollment and demand in the welding program. This move aims to better prepare students for technical careers by giving them access to modern tools needed in their fields.
“We need to continue to give students in each career field the biggest opportunity to pursue a high-quality education that prepares them for success,” Flick said. “I have helped secure funding for the Lycoming Career and Technology Center’s expansion of welding and other programs in the past, and I’m proud to see this funding reaffirm the Commonwealth’s confidence in the program.”
Hamm said, “Giving more students an opportunity to get into programs to receive excellent technical education is very important to me. Lycoming Career and Technology Center is producing the future workforce we need for critical jobs in our community, region and commonwealth. I was honored to support this funding for LycoCTC.”
The school is one of ten across Pennsylvania selected through the Manufacturing PA Training-to-Career Grant Program. The center is currently undergoing a multi-phase expansion project expected to add new programs such as welding and diesel technology, relocate its early childhood education program into its main facility, and increase capacity by about 150 students.
Flick represents the 83rd Legislative District in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives; he has also volunteered as a mentor for foster children, coached youth sports, founded Susquehanna Software—the top human services software provider in Pennsylvania—and sponsored legislation on child custody law reform promoting fairness and shared parenting. He was raised on his family’s farm, has six children (two serving in the United States military), according to the official website .
